q: The entropy rate of a stationary process (Xₙ) is defined as h = lim (1/n)H(X₁,...,Xₙ). This limit exists because:
opts: The conditional entropies H(Xₙ|X_{n-1},...,X₁) are non-increasing (subadditivity of entropy)
By the law of large numbers
exp: Subadditivity: H(X₁,...,Xₙ) ≤ ∑H(Xᵢ), so (1/n)H(X₁,...,Xₙ) is bounded. The sequence is also non-increasing: H(Xₙ|X₁,...,Xₙ₋₁) decreases as more conditioning information is added. By Cesàro, the limit equals lim H(Xₙ|X₁,...,Xₙ₋₁).
